**The control panel was rebuilt.** Same app, same overlay, same 30–45 MB — but the settings are no longer a single scroll with forty switches on it.

```
sha256  release  b39630eaff1a294c39a53bbafaacaf44b3b045e5c42e137776f5f0734581fd56
sha256  debug    8e74b3b1bbc04ecb40ad21f116431ee49030b3898253544de564304d76018c69
```

A phone browser that lands on a GitHub *page* instead of the file saves an HTML error page under the `.apk` name, and the installer then calls it corrupt — the size column is the quickest tell. Both APKs are signed with APK Signature Scheme v2 and verify with `apksigner verify` across API 24 to 34.

---

## What changed

### The tab bar floats

Three icons in a rounded pill that sits above the content instead of a full-width bar welded to the bottom edge. The active tab rides in a coloured circle that slides between them — and stretches slightly as it travels, so it reads as something with weight rather than a circle teleporting.

Labels are gone. Three destinations with distinct shapes don't need them, and dropping them buys the height that makes the bar look like a control rather than a toolbar. The list now runs *under* the pill instead of being guillotined by it.

### Categories, not one long scroll

The first screen of the Cards tab is now short: a header, the master switch, setup, and four category rows — **System events**, **Live cards**, **Gestures**, **Notifications** — each showing a strip of the icons it contains and opening its own screen.

That's the whole reorganisation. The top level answers "what can this thing do"; only the level below it asks you to make forty decisions. Each detail screen slides in from the right with its own title, a back arrow, and a **Guide** button that explains what the category is actually for.

### Switches say it twice

Every toggle now carries a **tick when it's on and a cross when it's off**, on a thumb that slides between them.

Colour alone is the one channel a colour-blind user doesn't have and a bright screen washes out. A tick and a cross say it a second way, and the second way survives both.

### Every row has an icon

Around forty icons, all drawn on a Canvas rather than loaded — one class, no resource lookups, and no `Drawable` objects held for rows that are off screen. They're tinted by *category*, never by state, so a screenful can be scanned by colour while the glyph inside still says what each row is.

### A new palette

The old one was near-black with a hard iOS blue: every card edge disappeared into the background and every accent shouted. Cards now sit a clear step above the background so a list reads as a list, and the accent is a periwinkle quiet enough to head every section without becoming the loudest thing on the page.

### The other two tabs were rebuilt to match

Island and Settings were still the old card style, which would have made the app look like two apps stitched together. Both are now built from the same six shapes — section header, card, toggle row, value row, nav row, note. Notification mode, auto-hide delay and "show only on the island" moved out of scattered corners and into the Notifications screen, where they belong.

---

## What did *not* change

The island itself. Same overlay, same geometry, same Canvas drawing, same behaviour on your camera cutout. This release is the app you configure it from.

Memory is unchanged at **30–45 MB**. The rebuild does not cost more: rows are ordinary Views built from one vocabulary, only the pieces that actually animate are hand-drawn, and roughly forty vector drawables became one class.

Still exactly **six permissions**. No `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`. **No `INTERNET`** — this app has never made a network request and cannot.

---

## Verified before release

- `clean assembleRelease assembleDebug lintDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL, zero lint errors**, and zero unused resources
- Both APKs `apksigner verify` → **VERIFIED**, API 24 through 34
- Manifest: six permissions, no `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES`, no `INTERNET`, all four activities present
- Every `findViewById` in the control panel audited against the layouts that are actually inflated — a stale id after a rewrite this size is a null at runtime, not a compile error
- Web demo: **31 browser assertions**, all 23 presentations through compact *and* expanded in both cutout shapes, each measured for clipped text
- Support page: **9 assertions**, the first being "issues zero requests" — now committed as `tools/test-support.js` and part of `npm test`

## Not verified

**The APK has never been launched on a phone.** The build machine has no KVM, so no emulator can boot on it — everything above is structural and static. This release rewrote most of the UI, so the first install is a genuine test rather than a formality. If something looks wrong on your device, that's a real finding.
